## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `15f8d1359d01b24ba9bf6e85d61deb7659d5f7f7`
Local-runs: none
Scope: .claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/contract-review.md, .claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/dispatch-runbook.md, .claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/lanes/review.md + scripts/pm/post-stamped.mjs, scripts/pm/check-skill-line-ratchet.mjs

Inputs read: card 33157 (body and both comments: claim 6879512661, os-dev-report 6879907765), PR 33287 (body, 5-file list, net diff +82 / -5 against `main`, no PR comments, no reviews), and the check-runs on this head. Code outside the diff was read at this head, never reviewed: `readMailboxLine`, `MAILBOX_KEYS` and the hand-off reader in `scripts/pm/record-recognisers.mjs`, `seatKey` in `scripts/pm/mailbox-open.mjs`, SKILL.md, `instrument-discipline.md`, `lanes/skills.md`, `execution-duties.md`, `project-forms.md`, `untrusted-text.md`, the header of `check-skill-id-lint.mjs`.

### ① Derived judgments

- Accept set of the write tool: `judgeBody` in comment mode now refuses one more body shape, a comment `readMailboxLine` reads as `request:contract-review` whose canonical `to` starts `triage#`. RIGHT as derived: nothing published narrows, the module ships in no package, and every other key to triage and every card body keep passing (pinned by the battery).
- Public surface: two new exports on an internal script (`triageContractReviewKnock`, `triageContractReviewKnockText`) and one more import from `record-recognisers.mjs`. No package export map moves. RIGHT.
- Rule surface: the 429-only hand-off line becomes the one route (self-review only when the lane can take the tier; otherwise review seat, then a sibling seat with the tier, else the owed-review list; never triage). This WIDENS when a hand-off is owed (account cannot reach the tier, maintainer rationing) and is the card's ordered change. RIGHT. It agrees with what `main` already encodes: the key table's `to` column for `request:contract-review` names a review seat or a sibling seat only, and the hand-off reader's target grammar already matches no `triage`.
- Governed tier: the card's Reader line says Tier H; the queue guard's reading of the committed tree is Tier S (three `.claude/**` paths; the two `scripts/pm` files are off the register). The tree decides, not the card: Tier S is RIGHT, and the `Governed Surface Queue Guard` check-run on this head concluded success.
- Ratchet: `contract-review.md` is 65 lines and `dispatch-runbook.md` 246 at this head, equal to the two raised ceilings (headroom 0); `lanes/review.md` stays 21. The arithmetic is RIGHT (+6 -1 = +5; +1). Whether all five lines are ordered is judged in ④.
- Check-runs on this head when this record was written: none failing. Concluded success include `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `PR-body guards`, `Check Changeset`, `Check PR Size`, `Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests`, `Lint · repo & tooling gates`, `Lint · docs & code guards`, `Lint · ESLint`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Lint · CI, release & engine gates`, all four `Type Check` jobs and `Test Core (2/8)`. STILL IN PROGRESS: `Test Core (1/8)`. This PASS does not stand in for it: the seat reads its conclusion before it queues, and a red there outranks this record.

### ② Semver level

`skip-changeset` is right: the diff touches `.claude/**` and `scripts/pm/**` only, and no package publishes either. `Check Changeset` concluded success.

Clause-②: no — correct. No published accept set, schema, error code or runtime capability changes; the refusal narrows only what an internal write tool will post, so the `(narrowing)` arm does not apply. `Metadata-protocol: none` is correct.

### ③ Boundary flags

`open_questions` is empty. The dev's four out-of-scope flags, each answered:

- Reading of the default-no line for new gates (SKILL.md, the fourth axis): ANSWERED, not escalated. I take the INPUT-CHECK reading. Reasons, from the tree: (1) `instrument-discipline.md` defines a hard gate by what it answers (governed register, queue guard, CI test, whether a review record exists), and its add-rule lists gates, patrol rows and ratchets; a write tool's refusal of its own act is none of the three. (2) SKILL.md's lane table files these scripts as the non-gate `scripts/pm/**` loop tools, and `seat-post-protocol.md` already names this class in its own words (a missing signature is refused by the write tool). (3) No landing, check-run, workflow, label or queue guard reads the refusal; a seat with another write path is not stopped, so it cannot hold a PR. (4) It introduces no new rule: `never triage` was already contract on `main` in the key table's `to` column and in the hand-off reader; the refusal applies the existing addressee column at write time. On the other reading it would be a must-fix, because the maintainer's words quoted on the card name the ROUTE and not a mechanical refusal (item 3 of the card is the triage seat's sentence). The honest residue: a no-flag exit-2 refusal with a floored self-test battery is gate-like to the one writer it stops. The seat's ACCEPT should name which reading it adopts; the function and its one `judgeBody` line drop cleanly if the maintainer reads it the other way.
- Card item 2 implemented as one runbook line, `os-dev.md` untouched: ACCEPTED as a declared deviation. The claim's file surface allows either file. Note the PR body's reason is overstated: `os-dev.md` at this head says nothing about mailboxes at all, so it does not forbid a dev knock; what stops one is the order's line and the write tool's refusal.
- `execution-duties.md` untouched: ACCEPTED. Its tier-policy lines say how a seat takes the tier and when a build may step down; none names whom to ask for a review, so nothing there restates or contradicts the route.
- Card item 4 (retire the morning seat ruling in seat posts): not in this diff, carried to the seat with the dev's reading (no seat post body carries it; two long threads not read comment by comment). The seat owns it; nothing here depends on it.
- Tier S against the card's Tier H: answered in ①.
- Author note: the PR's `user.login` is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`, so no off-relay author note is owed.
- Ruling carrier: the maintainer's four lines reach this PR as the triage seat's transcription in the card body (who, verbatim words, where: the triage seat's session). `untrusted-text.md` accepts a fleet transcription carrying those three items as the ruling's carrier. The quotations in the diff and in the PR body match the card body character for character. There is no ruling COMMENT id to quote; the PR cites the card body and claim comment 6879512661, the same form the 241 to 245 raise on `dispatch-runbook.md` used.

### ④ Design judgment

`contract-review.md` (hits)

- The route itself (new lines 21 to 23) HOLDS against the card's scenario and the code it leans on: the three ways a lane lacks the tier are named, the no-step-down and never-triage bars are explicit, the knock rides the same stroke as the hand-off line, and the neither-seat case lands on the owed-review list, where rule (a) is met by the waiting marker alone. The hand-off template line is byte-identical, so the self-test pin in `record-recognisers.mjs` holds, and its tail reader takes any reason text, so a rationed or unreachable tier is spellable.
- SHOULD-FIX 1 — the provenance block (new lines 25 to 27) quotes four maintainer lines, and the last one is the SUPERSEDED arrangement: verbatim, it says contract review comes to "you" (the triage seat it was spoken to) when a lane has no fable. Printed in the rule file with no marker that it is superseded and no referent for "you", it states the opposite of the route two lines above it, in the maintainer's own voice, to every seat that reads the file. A second quote is conversational context, not a criterion. This also sits against the file's own history: the ceiling comment directly above the raise records the maintainer-ordered rules-only rewrite that took provenance narrative OUT of this file (68 to 60), and the id-lint header states the corpus standard as rules only, with provenance in the landing PR. Landed precedent elsewhere in the corpus is one provenance line holding the operative words. Fix: keep one line with the operative quote(s) and the card pointer, drop the superseded and the contextual quote, and lower the raise to what remains.
- NIT — the trailing colon that used to introduce the hand-off template now follows "(a)(b)(c)", so the template bullet reads as if it expanded those rules; in the neither-seat case the template has no addressee and only the marker applies, which the sentence leaves the reader to infer.

`lanes/review.md` (hits)

- HOLDS. The route line now points at the one home and keeps only the seat's own half (any review seat's mailbox, the idle one takes it). Nothing the old line said is lost: the sibling fallback and the never-triage bar both live in the pointed-at line, and line 14 of the charter (owed list first to the review seat) still agrees.

`dispatch-runbook.md` (hits)

- HOLDS as a rule for the seat that builds the order: the order carries the route, the dev names the owed review and does not knock, the seat routes. Against the card's own incident (dev sub-sessions knocking triage because they never read the seat's mailbox) it works only together with the refusal below, which is what actually teaches a sub-session the route.
- NIT — "the seat sends it to a review seat" compresses the route: a seat that can take the tier self-reviews. The pointer to `contract-review.md` saves it, but the line read alone says otherwise. NIT — unlike its neighbours it gives no wording for the sentence the order carries.

`scripts/pm/post-stamped.mjs` (implementing)

- Agrees with the contract sentence by sentence on the knock it reads: the reader is imported, not restated; `seatKey` canonicalises the seat, so a bare `triage` and any case or seat number match `^triage#`; the check runs inside `judgeBody` on comments only, so `label-write.mjs --comment-file` inherits it; the return shape matches the refusals beside it; the refusal text names the review seat's mailbox, the sibling fallback, the owed-review list and the rule's home, and carries no tracker number. The battery's nine cases equal its declared floor.
- SHOULD-FIX 2 — the refusal covers only a knock in state `read`. `readMailboxLine` returns `unreadable` (with no `to` and no key) for a KNOWN key whose line misses its template or is followed by a second line of content, so a knock addressed to triage with `Request: contract-review` and a missing reason field, a PR number without its `#`, or one explanatory line under it is posted to the triage mailbox unrefused. That is exactly the shape a sub-session that has not read the key table writes, which is the card's named offender; the card's item 3 sentence (a `To:` triage seat and the key `Request: contract-review`) is true of that knock, and the card's acceptance (no contract-review knocks reach triage) is not met for it. The patrol's half-state row then costs triage the read the card set out to remove. No battery case pins the pass-through either, so the boundary is stated in jsdoc only. Fix without restating the reader: have the reader's `unreadable` answer carry the `to` and key it has already parsed, and refuse on them; or, if the boundary is kept on purpose, pin it with a case and say so in the usage text.
- NIT — the check fires on any comment shaped as a knock, wherever it is posted, including a blockquoted knock quoted alone (the key-line convention treats a blockquote as decoration). Harmless today; worth one sentence in the jsdoc.
- NIT (follow-up, outside the diff) — the hand-off reader's jsdoc in `record-recognisers.mjs` still says the seat hands over ONLY on a quota refusal; the rule now names three cases. The reader's behaviour is unaffected.

`scripts/pm/check-skill-line-ratchet.mjs` (implementing)

- The two rows move in the same PR by exactly the measured deltas, each comment carries the maintainer's verbatim words, the card and the claim comment id, and the PR body repeats both with the deltas (+5, +1). The words are verbatim against the card body. `dispatch-runbook.md` +1 is BACKED: one line the route needs. `contract-review.md`: +2 for the rule is BACKED by the ordering words; the +3 for provenance is backed only by the card's instruction to quote, not by the maintainer's words, and the header's rule is that a line no ruling ordered is paid for by deletion. It resolves with should-fix 1: the ceiling follows the trimmed provenance down (63 or 64), and the row comment and the PR body restate the delta.

Findings: 0 must-fix, 2 should-fix, 5 nit. The two should-fix items earn a delta review of their fix on the new head by this reviewer; the nits are left as accepted deviations or a follow-up card.

**VERDICT: PASS**

Delta review of round 1, and a full record for this head. Inputs read: card 33157 (body and all four comments: claim 6879512661, os-dev-reports 6879907765 and 6880395481, the earlier record 6880051283 on the previous head), PR 33287 (body as patched, 6-file list, net diff +89 / -8 against `main`, the delta from the previous head `15f8d135`, no PR comments), and the check-runs on this head. Code outside the diff was read at this head, never reviewed: `h72OffTableMailboxLines` and its sweep in `scripts/pm/check-half-states.mjs`, `seatKey` in `scripts/pm/mailbox-open.mjs`, and the rule files read for the earlier record.

### ① Derived judgments

- Accept set of the write tool: `judgeBody` in comment mode refuses a comment the doorbell reader reads OR finds unreadable as `request:contract-review` with a canonical `to` starting `triage#`. RIGHT: wider than the previous head by exactly the malformed knocks, still an internal tool, nothing published narrows; a comment the reader refuses outright (no `To:` seat, a key outside the table) passes as before.
- Reader surface: the `unreadable` answer of `readMailboxLine` gains `id`, `key` and `to`. ADDITIVE and RIGHT: no field is removed or renamed, no state changes, and the `refused` and `read` answers are byte-for-byte as they were. The move of the `unreadable` helper below the table lookup is safe: it was never called before that point, and `to` and `entry` are both non-null there.
- Rule surface: unchanged in substance from the previous head (one route; review seat, then a sibling seat with the tier, else the owed-review list; never triage). RIGHT.
- Governed tier: Tier S from the committed tree (three `.claude/**` paths; the three `scripts/pm` files are off the register). `Governed Surface Queue Guard` concluded success on this head.
- Ratchet: `contract-review.md` is 63 lines, `dispatch-runbook.md` 246, `lanes/review.md` 21 at this head; the two ceilings read 63 and 246, headroom 0. RIGHT.
- Check-runs on this head: every run is completed; none failed and none is pending. Concluded success include `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, both `PR-body guards` runs, `Check PR Size`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests`, `Lint · repo & tooling gates`, `Lint · CI, release & engine gates`, `Lint · docs & code guards`, `Lint · ESLint`, the four `Type Check` jobs, `Test Core (1/8)`, `Test Core (2/8)` and the `Test Core` roll-up. The rest are skipped, `Check Changeset` among them (both of its runs on this head concluded skipped).

### ② Semver level

`skip-changeset` is right: `.claude/**` and `scripts/pm/**` only, published by no package. `Check Changeset` concluded skipped on this head, so the label and this reading carry it, not a green run.

Clause-②: no — correct. No published accept set, schema, error code or runtime capability changes; the `(narrowing)` arm does not apply. `Metadata-protocol: none` is correct.

### ③ Boundary flags

`open_questions` is empty in both dev reports. Flags, each answered:

- Round-1 deviation, `scripts/pm/record-recognisers.mjs` joins the diff outside the claim's listed file surface: ACCEPTED. It is the fix the earlier record asked for (the reader hands over what it already parsed, so the write tool restates nothing), the dev named it, and the `PR-body guards` single-writer-path run is green on this head. The seat's ACCEPT should name the widened surface.
- Round-1 deviation, the dev left the PR body to the seat: ANSWERED. The body on the PR now carries the round-1 text: 60 to 63 with +3, 771 and 383 cases, the malformed-knock case, and `record-recognisers.mjs` in the off-register list.
- Reading of the default-no line for new gates: unchanged from the earlier record. I take the INPUT-CHECK reading (a write tool refusing its own act; filed by SKILL.md as a non-gate loop tool; read by no landing, check, workflow, label or queue guard; `never triage` was already contract on `main` in the key table's `to` column and the hand-off reader). Widening the refusal to malformed knocks does not change its class. On the gate reading it would be a must-fix, since the maintainer's quoted words name the route and not a mechanical refusal; the seat's ACCEPT names the reading it adopts.
- Card item 2 as one runbook line, `execution-duties.md` untouched, card item 4 carried to the seat, Tier S against the card's Tier H: all as answered in the earlier record; nothing in the delta moves them.
- Author note: the PR's `user.login` is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; no off-relay note is owed.
- Ruling carrier: the two quotations kept in the rule file, the ceiling comment and the PR body match the card body character for character; the citation form (card body plus claim comment 6879512661) is the one the earlier raise on `dispatch-runbook.md` used.

### ④ Design judgment

Earlier should-fix 1 (superseded quote in the provenance block): FIXED. The block is one line with the two operative quotes; the superseded arrangement and the contextual quote are gone, and the ceiling came down with them.

Earlier should-fix 2 (malformed triage knock passed): FIXED. The reader's `unreadable` answer carries the key and seat it parsed, the write tool refuses on them without a parser of its own, and a battery case pins a missing reason, a bare PR number and a second line, plus the same malformed knock to a review seat passing.

`contract-review.md` (hits)

- HOLDS. The route paragraph now ends on the words that introduce the hand-off template, the neither-seat case says to hang the waiting marker (which is what meets rule (a) with no addressee), and the template line is byte-identical, so the reader's verbatim pin holds.
- NIT — the provenance line is two bare quotations and a card number: the label, the speaker and the date that every other provenance line in the corpus carries are gone, so the file no longer says whose words they are. The ceiling comment and the card do.
- NIT — the review-seat path no longer says to keep the waiting marker (the old line did). No rule is lost: the marker section of the same file hangs it at ACCEPT and takes it off only on a PASS, a merge or a close.

`lanes/review.md` (hits)

- HOLDS, unchanged since the earlier record: a pointer to the one route line plus the seat's own half.

`dispatch-runbook.md` (hits)

- HOLDS. The line now names self-review beside the review seat, so it reads correctly alone. NIT (carried) — it still gives no wording for the sentence the order carries.

`scripts/pm/record-recognisers.mjs` (implementing)

- Agrees with its jsdoc and breaks no other reader. `readMailboxLine` has two consumers in the tree: `mailboxEvents` in the same file, and through it the H72 patrol row, plus the write tool. H72 filters on `state` alone and prints `state`, `reason`, `comment` and `by`; it never reads `id`, `key` or `to`, so its findings are identical. `mailboxEvents` spreads the reading and stamps the comment id as `comment`, not `id`, so the new `id` on an unreadable event shadows nothing, and `halfStates` is still computed from `state`. No workflow or other script imports either function. The new case pins `id`, `key`, `kind` and `to` on two unreadable shapes.
- NIT — an event list now holds unreadable rows that carry a key `id`. No consumer today selects events by `id` without `state`, but one written later that did would count a malformed bell as rung; one sentence on `mailboxEvents` would say so.

`scripts/pm/post-stamped.mjs` (implementing)

- Agrees with the contract sentence by sentence: read or unreadable, a `request:contract-review` knock whose seat canonicalises to `triage#N` is refused; `refused` readings pass; comments only; the usage text says the template need not be spelled. The battery holds ten cases against a declared floor of ten. The refusal text is unchanged and still names the review seat's mailbox, the sibling fallback, the owed-review list and the rule's home.
- NIT (carried) — the check fires on any comment shaped as a knock wherever it is posted, including a lone blockquoted one.

`scripts/pm/check-skill-line-ratchet.mjs` (implementing)

- BOTH RAISES BACKED. `contract-review.md` 60 to 63: the row comment carries the maintainer's two verbatim lines, the card and the claim comment id, and prices the delta as the rule (+2) and one provenance line (+1), measured +3, equal to the file's count. `dispatch-runbook.md` 245 to 246: one ordered line, measured +1. The PR body repeats both rulings and both deltas. The row moved down from the previous head by lowering, which needs no ruling.

Findings: 0 must-fix, 0 should-fix, 5 nit (two new, three carried). Nits alone end the round: they are left as accepted deviations or a follow-up card, since a fix on these files would move the head.
